Every doc I've ever submitted has always said you were born on Fest.|Maarva Andor, to Cassian Andor|{{Andor|That Would Be Me}}}} '''Fest''' was a [[Temperature|cold]], [[mountain]]ous [[planet]] located in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]' [[Atrivis sector]]. It was the [[Forger (profession)|forged]] [[homeworld]] of the adopted [[Gender|boy]] Kassa, later renamed [[Cassian Jeron Andor]]. The [[Galactic Empire]] occupied Fest's industrial zones and forced many of the local [[human]]s to work there. The Empire ultimately savaged the world, and [[refugee]]s were taken in by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] [[Great Temple|base]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]]. ==Description== Fest was a backwater [[planet]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' located in an [[Fest system|eponymous star system]] within an intersecting portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories]] and the [[New Territories]]. Situated in the [[Atrivis sector]] at the coordinates L-5 on the [[Standard Galactic Grid]], it was linked by a [[hyperspace route]] to''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' the planet [[Dantooine]]. It was a [[Temperature|cold]] world with many [[mountain]]s. ==History== {{Quote|Cassian Andor. This says he's from Fest.''"
"''This was a tip call, right? Probably someone messing with us.''"
"''I don't see Kenari here.|Two Corporate Authority officers|}} [[File:Cassian_field_jacket.png|thumb|left|250px|Fest was the forged homeworld of Cassian Andor (pictured).]] In the [[Republic Era|latter years]] of the [[Galactic Republic]],{{SW|url=andor-s1-e3-trivia-gallery|text="Reckoning" Trivia Gallery | Andor}} {{C|Slide 1}} prior to [[22 BBY]],{{SW|url=andor-s1-e3-trivia-gallery|text="Reckoning" Trivia Gallery | Andor}} {{C|Slide 1}} states that the scenes on [[Kenari]] in "[[Reckoning (episode)|Reckoning]]" took place prior to the [[Clone Wars]], which started in [[22 BBY]], according to ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''. the [[Gender|boy]] [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Kassa]] was taken off his [[homeworld]] of [[Kenari]] by the [[scavenger]]s [[Maarva Carassi Andor|Maarva Andor]] and [[Clem Andor]], who believed the Republic would slaughter his [[Alpha (Kenari)|tribe]].{{Andor|Reckoning (episode)}} Raising the boy under the name "Cassian Jeron Andor,"''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' Maarva [[Forger (profession)|made sure]] to list his homeworld as Fest in every document she submitted. At the end of the [[Clone Wars]], which lasted from 22 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]] to [[19 BBY]], the Republic [[Proclamation of the New Order|became]] the [[Galactic Empire]]. The successor [[Politics|government]] occupied Fest's industrial zones, forcing many of the world's [[human]] denizens to labor there. In [[5 BBY]], Cassian Andor [[Death|murdered]] two [[Tac-Corpo|sentry guards]] from the{{Andor|Kassa (episode)}} [[Pre-Mor Authority Security Forces]] on the planet [[Morlana One]].''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' Beforehand, he had mistakenly revealed to a [[Unidentified brothel hostess|local hostess]] that he was from Kenari, and the information then found its way to Pre-Mor Enforcement. When the [[Law enforcement agency|authority]] was tipped off about Andor being the [[Kenari (people)|Kenari]] male suspect, a group of [[officer]]s checked Andor's record and became skeptical upon learning Fest was indicated as his homeworld. The hostess was nevertheless brought in and identified Andor as the killer. Despite the Imperial presence, Fest became an operations headquarters for an [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|organized rebellion]] that was secretly led by [[Senator]] [[Mon Mothma]] by [[2 BBY]].In ''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'', the report regarding the rebel locations that included Fest is set between the introduction of the [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter]] and the [[Declaration of the Rebel Alliance]], which are both dated to [[2 BBY]] by ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''. As such, the world was noted on a [[Star map|map]] of [[the galaxy]] sent to Mothma that listed rebel [[safe world]]s, [[starfighter]] hubs at level five or higher, operations headquarters, [[shadow planet]]s, and deep [[Realspace|space]] caches. [[Archivist]] [[Hendri Underholt]] included the [[map]] in the non-electronic archive known as ''[[The Rebel Files]]''. The rebellion was [[Declaration of the Rebel Alliance|formalized]] in 2 BBY as the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]], and Fest ultimately became savaged under the Empire, bleeding [[refugee]]s that were welcomed to the Alliance [[Great Temple|base]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]].{{StoryCite|story=By Whatever Sun|book=From a Certain Point of View}} ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|There was some apocryphal information he was from Fest and whatever, and oh well let me turn that upside down. Where is he from?|Tony Gilroy, on the situation of Cassian Andor's homeworld|{{SWYouTube|VyIHhK2VKvQ|Star Wars Celebration LIVE! 2023 - DAY 1}}}} [[File:Fest_transport.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Fest, as it appears in ''Star Wars'' Legends]] Fest was introduced into the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] when it was mentioned simultaneously in [[Jason Fry]]'s young-readers book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission]]''''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission]]'' and [[Pablo Hidalgo]]'s reference book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', both released on [[December 16]], [[2016]].{{SW|url=news/rebel-reading-rogue-one-books|text=Rebel Reading: A Guide to ''Rogue One'' Books}} Originating in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Fest/Legends|Fest]] was introduced in [[West End Games]]' ''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]'', written by [[Paul Murphy]] and published in [[1990]] as part of ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. Artist [[Allen Nunis]] illustrated the world in that sourcebook.''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]'' Fest first appeared in Legends in the [[1995]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]'', developed by [[LucasArts]].''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]'' ''Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission'' and ''Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide'' establish that Cassian Andor's homeworld was Fest. This information was repeated in later sources;''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission]]''''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]''{{HelmetCollectionCite|56|Weapons & Uniforms}}''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia, New Edition]]''''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''{{EncyclopediaCite|The Heroes of Rogue One}}''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' however, "[[That Would Be Me]]"—the second episode of the [[Andor Season 1|first season]] of [[Tony Gilroy]]'s live-action [[Disney+]] series ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'' that was released on [[September 21]], [[2022]]{{InsiderCite|217|Star Wars: Andor Season One Companion|''Star Wars: Andor'' Season One Companion}}—established this was an [[in-universe]] lie that Maarva Andor had fabricated, and that Cassian's actual homeworld was Kenari. The 2023 reference book ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' mistakenly repeats as supposed fact the outdated information that Andor was from Fest. While speaking at a panel on the first day of [[Celebration Europe (2023)|Celebration Europe]] on [[April 7]], [[2023]], Gilroy revealed that, when creating a homeworld for Andor, he saw the pre-existing information on Fest and chose to "turn [it] upside down." In another interview, Gilroy reminisced that he had not liked that Andor had Fest as a homeworld as it did not fit with the story he wanted to tell. As a result, when thinking of how to explain away canonical entries mentioning Andor's homeworld, he noted that it was decided to make it so Andor was trying to hide his origins in-universe. Gilroy indicated that weaving the lie about Fest into the scene in which Andor and Maarva discuss the issue was done to further develop the concept that he was disappointing his mother, as he had ended up revealing his secret, real homeworld. He was happy with the result, believing that the mention of Fest was able to further develop the characters by pushing the scene along to reveal more of Andor's personality.{{YouTube|video=X13nYZNTLYM|text=Andor Q&A - Tony Gilroy - (S1 eps 1-4 )|channel=backstorymagazine2757|name=Backstory Magazine|date=2022-09-29}} ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Fest}} *{{Andor|That Would Be Me}} {{Mo}} *{{Andor|Reckoning (episode)}} {{Mo}} *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission]]'' {{1stm|''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''}} *{{StoryCite|story=By Whatever Sun|book=From a Certain Point of View|audiobook=1}} {{Mo}} ==Sources== *''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' *{{HelmetCollectionCite|56|Weapons & Uniforms}} *''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia, New Edition]]'' *''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' *{{EncyclopediaCite|The Heroes of Rogue One}} *''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' *{{InsiderCite|212|From the Shadows: The Dangerous Life of a Rebel Agent}} *{{SW|url=news/cassian-andor-101-the-story-of-a-rebel|text=Cassian Andor 101: The Story of a Rebel|nolive=1}} *{{SW|url=series/andor/andor-season-1-episode-2-episode-guide|text="That Would Be Me" Episode Guide | Andor}} *{{SW|url=news/andor-episode-2-that-would-be-me-highlights|text=''Andor'' Analyzed: 5 Highlights from Episode 2, "That Would Be Me"}} *{{SWYouTube|VyIHhK2VKvQ|Star Wars Celebration LIVE!
